subject: Urban Planning
title: The Missing Middle: Housing That Doesn't Exist
description: Learn The Missing Middle: Housing That Doesn't Exist in one minute.

hook.text: America builds single-family homes and large towers. The middle — duplexes, fourplexes, courtyard buildings — barely exists.

buildup.text: Missing middle housing fits 4-20 units on a residential lot. It's walkable, neighborhood-scaled, and affordable.

discovery.text: Zoning banned these building types in most cities starting in the 1940s. They were legal everywhere before that.

twist.text: The most beloved neighborhoods — brownstone Brooklyn, bungalow courts in LA — are all missing middle housing.

climax.text: Oregon legalized missing middle housing statewide in 2019. California and Washington followed. The trend is accelerating.

punchline.text: The housing people love most is the housing zoning won't allow.

quiz.question: What is 'missing middle' housing?
options: Affordable housing for middle-income families specifically
Building types between single-family homes and large towers, like duplexes and fourplexes
Housing built in the center of a city between downtown and suburbs
